subject: general
question: A dealer purchased an AC for ₹1,848. After allowing a discount of 58% on its marked price, he still gains 63%. Find the marked price of the AC.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost price = 1848

Gain 63% ⇒ SP = 1848 × 1.63 = 3012.24

Discount 58% ⇒ SP = 42% of MP

MP = 3012.24 ÷ 0.42

**∴ Answer = ₹7172**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price = 1848

Gain = 63%

Discount = 58%

**Formula used:**

Selling Price = CP × (1 + Gain/100)

Selling Price = MP × (1 − Discount/100)

**Calculation:**

⇒ SP = 1848 × (1 + 63/100)

⇒ SP = 1848 × 163/100

⇒ SP = 3012.24

⇒ SP = MP × (1 − 58/100)

⇒ SP = MP × 42/100

⇒ 3012.24 = MP × 42/100

⇒ MP = (3012.24 × 100) ÷ 42

⇒ MP = 7172

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7172.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price Concept

Marked Price is the listed price before discount. SP = MP × (1 − discount/100)

Profit Formula

Profit = SP − CP, and SP = CP × (1 + profit/100)

Successive Effect

Discount and profit act on different bases (MP and CP respectively)

Reverse Calculation Trick

First find SP using profit, then back-calculate MP using discount
